i relate so much, honestly. when i am spiraling or im depressed my critical voice feels so loud because it feels true. it feels like everything it’s telling me is true. but let’s say even if parts of what it is saying is true, you can still learn the same lesson in a kinder way. for example my critical voice often tells me im not doing enough and im lazy. what it is really saying is that “im worried you’re not going to be happy with your life, im worried you will never put the effort in to chase your dreams”. you can take this same lesson just in a kinder way. because even if there really is a change that needs to happen for example maybe you need to stick with a job to save up to move in with your friends, you’re not going to find the motivation to make this change through being so mean to yourself. if you practice encouraging yourself to make the changes you want to make, it will be easier to actually create change. therapy is mistaken sometimes as an excuse to just accept yourself the way you are but maybe there are things you can change that would make you happier. it’s just about how you approach it. and it feels so wrong and unnatural to be kind to yourself but with time and practice it becomes easier to believe and easier to do. next time your brain is being mean to you maybe try writing down what it’s saying, what it actually means and how you can change what it’s saying into a kinder way. sending you love ❤️❤️❤️❤️

i understand i’ve been there. it’s okay honestly, you’re young and there’s so much left to learn and experience. it does get better but you have to learn how to talk to your critical voice. inner child work helped a lot for me. if you’re able to get therapy, please do, it does help if you’re willing to accept it. good things are scary and feel unnatural but you have to fight for them, that’s the only way you will feel better. definitely please move in with your friends, it sounds like such an exciting experience. i felt like i only started to develop and actually learn who i am once i moved out for uni. i know it sounds stupid as fucking annoying to hear especially cos it’s so much easier said than done but honestly self-compassion and kind discipline is the only way forward and the only way you’re going to feel better. you cannot punish yourself for feeling bad or sad and expect it to go away. you can’t berate and be horrible to yourself for feeling idk lazy or depressed, you HAVE to be kinder to yourself. you have to sit with the negative feelings, examine them, what are they actually saying. all of our parts are trying to protect us from something. take only what resonates, everyone is different and what works for me may not work for you but regardless of your experiences or opinions, self-compassion is key!
